# Welcome to Fin# (`Financial Sharp` / `finsc`) {#welcome}

**Fin# (`Financial Sharp`, `.fin`)** is RaggieSoft Labs' open-source (**MIT License**), linear-type double-entry financial programming language and `.NET` compiler blueprint where **the First Law of Thermodynamics is enforced on money at compile time**.

> [!TIP] Press `Ctrl+K` (or `/`) anywhere on **finsharp.raggiesoft.dev** to search every linear type (`Capital<T>`, `Account<K, T>`), standard library function, `finsc` CLI command, and `FIN0001`–`FIN0005` diagnostic, or browse the [Master A–Z API Index](api-index.html). Curious how a novel chapter inspired a real compiler? Read [Origin Story: From `/books/aubrie` Plot Device to Real Language](origin-in-aubrie.html).

## Why Imperative Languages Fail Accounting {#why-imperative-fails}

In mainstream imperative languages—C#, Java, C++, Python, TypeScript, and imperative spreadsheet macros—monetary balances are represented as ordinary unconstrained scalar numbers (`decimal`, `BigDecimal`, or worse, binary `double`).

In an unconstrained scalar language, the following line compiles with **zero warnings and zero errors**:

```csharp
// Standard imperative code: compiles cleanly even though $500,000,000.00
// just materialized out of thin air without debiting any counterparty account!
companyRevenue += 500_000_000.00m;
```

Even when engineering teams apply strict code reviews and Sarbanes-Oxley (`SOX` Sections 302 and 404) controls, scalar languages only discover unbalanced postings, dropped sub-cent rounding remainders, or accidental cross-currency additions **at runtime or months later during a forensic audit**.

**Fin# catches them in milliseconds at compile time.**

## The Five Compile-Time Conservation Laws of Fin# {#five-laws}

| Invariant | Compiler Diagnostic | What `finsc` Proves Before Emitting Code |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. No Thin-Air Mutation** | `FIN0001` | Scalar `+=`, `-=`, `=`, or un-paired account writes outside an atomic `transaction` block are rejected immediately. |
| **2. Balanced Double-Entry** | `FIN0002` | Every `transaction` block proves Luca Pacioli's 1494 identity ($\sum \text{Debits} \equiv \sum \text{Credits}$) per currency. |
| **3. Zero Binary Floating-Point** | `FIN0003` | IEEE 754 `float` and `double` cannot touch `Capital<T>`, `Rate<A, B>`, or `Account<K, T>`; all math is 128-bit scaled fixed-point. |
| **4. Dimension-Typed Currencies** | `FIN0004` | `Capital<USD>` and `Capital<EUR>` cannot be mixed without an explicit `fx.convert(...)` clearing bridge. |
| **5. Linear Remainder Safety** | `FIN0005` | `Capital<T>` is a linear resource (`Move`-only: no `Copy`, no silent `Drop`). Unallocated split remainders fail compilation! |

## 60-Second Tour: Your First `.fin` Ledger {#quick-tour}

Here is the real-world scene from *The Eleventh Child*—recording a \$30.00 annual aquatic center keytag pass on Geneva Street—written in idiomatic **Fin#**:

```rssc
// geneva_household.fin — Every cent is conserved at compile time!
ledger GenevaHousehold412 [currency: USD, audit_standard: Z_SOX_302] {
    account OperatingChecking : Account<Asset, USD>;
    account WellnessPassPool  : Account<Expense, USD>;
    account HouseholdEquity   : Account<Equity, USD>;

    // Explicit external boundary ingress: pairs Asset against Equity
    opening_balance(
        debit:  OperatingChecking,
        credit: HouseholdEquity,
        amount: 1_250.00_USD,
        memo:   "August 2015 Fall Semester Opening Balance"
    );

    // Atomic double-entry transaction: Sum(Debits) == Sum(Credits) == $30.00 USD
    transaction PurchaseAquaticKeytag [audit: Z_SOX_302, date: "2015-10-09"] {
        let keytagFee : Capital<USD> = credit OperatingChecking -> 30.00_USD;
        debit WellnessPassPool <- keytagFee;
    }
}
```

Try deleting `debit WellnessPassPool <- keytagFee;` in `PurchaseAquaticKeytag`:
- First, `finsc check` raises **`FIN0005` (`UnconsumedLinearCapitalError`)** because `keytagFee` (`Capital<USD>`) reached the end of its scope without being consumed into a destination account.
- Second, `finsc check` raises **`FIN0002` (`UnbalancedJournalEntryError`)** because the transaction has `30.00_USD` in credits and `0.00_USD` in debits!

# Narrative Origin: From `/books/aubrie` Plot Device to Real Language {#origin-story}

Most programming languages start in a corporate compiler lab or a university thesis committee. **Fin# (`Financial Sharp`)** started as a plot device around a fictional oak dining table in Christiansburg, Virginia—inside Michael P. Ragsdale's novel [***The Eleventh Child: The Story of Jordan***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie).

Long before Antigravity made it possible to architect full multi-target compilers and Help Studio documentation portals locally in `Y:\desktop-apps\`, Michael was co-developing the world of *The Eleventh Child* with Gemini on the Web. What began as an authentic, character-driven capstone idea for an autistic Computer Science and Finance double major turned out to have such a clean mathematical core—**applying linear resource types to Luca Pacioli's 1494 double-entry accounting identity**—that RaggieSoft Labs promoted `Fin#` into a real MIT-licensed language specification and `.NET` compiler project!

![Around the oak dining table on Geneva Street in Christiansburg, Zoë Wren Brooks and Jordan Fuller in his S.S. Freedom power wheelchair co-design the linear-type compiler for Fin# to enforce the First Law of Thermodynamics on double-entry accounting, while Daniel Brooks stands proudly behind Zoë and Aubrie Jean Kelly and Mark look on.](https://assets.raggiesoft.com/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c001/p003/birth-of-finsharp.jpg)

## August 26, 2015: *"Question The Rules"* on Geneva Street {#question-the-rules}

In [**Part 3: Question The Rules: The Birth of Fin#**](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie/fall-semester-2015/the-5-45-am-problem-the-birth-of-fin-home-on-geneva-street/part-3-question-the-rules-the-birth-of-fin) (`books/aubrie/e007/c001/p003.md`), sophomore double-major **Zoë Wren Brooks** sits at the Geneva Street dining table enrolled simultaneously in two courses at **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)**:

1. **CS 3214** — *Compiler Design & Programming Languages*
2. **ACIS 3115** — *Intermediate Financial Accounting & Corporate Governance*

Alongside her father **Daniel Brooks, CPA**, Zoë reviews a forensic accounting case study on the fictional December 2001 collapse of Houston-based **Vectron Energy Corp.**, whose late-1990s television commercials famously dared viewers to *"Question The Rules"* while executives hid debt off balance sheet—forcing the passage of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (`SOX`).

Sitting beside Zoë in his *S.S. Freedom* power wheelchair with his Engineering Thermodynamics textbook open, **Jordan Fuller** types the insight that sparks the entire language on his AAC device:

> *"In physics, you can question the rules of who owns the power lines, but you cannot question the First Law of Thermodynamics! Energy in a closed system cannot be created out of nothing or destroyed—it can only be transferred from one place to another."*
>
> *"Because rules made by monopolies can be questioned. The laws of conservation cannot."*

Zoë immediately connects Jordan's thermodynamics law to quantum no-cloning linear types and double-entry bookkeeping: if a programming language treats `Capital<USD>` as a **conserved linear state** rather than an overwriteable scalar number, an unbalanced off-balance-sheet entry cannot even compile (`FIN0001` / `FIN0002`).

# Linear Resource Types (`Capital<T>`, `Account<K, T>` & Move Semantics) {#capital-type}

The heart of **Fin#** is its **Linear Flow Analyzer** (`LinearFlowAnalyzer` in `FinSharp.Compiler`). Inspired by substructural linear logic (Girard, 1987) and quantum no-cloning / no-deleting theorems in `Q#`, Fin# splits data types into two worlds:

1. **Ordinary Unrestricted Value Types** (`Int64`, `String`, `Date`, `Bool`, `DecimalQuantity`): Can be copied, inspected, and dropped freely—just like values in C# or F#.
2. **Linear Monetary Resource Types** (`Capital<TCurrency>`): Represent conserved units of purchasing power or commodity obligation. Every `Capital<TCurrency>` binding **must be consumed exactly once** along every control-flow path!

## Rules of `Capital<TCurrency>` {#linear-rules}

A binding of type `Capital<USD>` obeys three compile-time substructural laws:

1. **No Implicit `Copy`**: Passing `payment` to `debit RentExpense <- payment;` *moves* ownership into the posting and marks `payment` as **Consumed**. Referencing `payment` a second time fails compilation!
2. **No Silent `Drop` (`FIN0005`)**: Allowing a `Capital<T>` variable—including an `if`/`else` branch or a `0.01_USD` split remainder—to go out of scope unconsumed fails compilation with **`FIN0005` (`UnconsumedLinearCapitalError`)**.
3. **No Unpaired Literal Minting (`FIN0001`)**: Outside a `transaction` credit leg or an explicit `opening_balance(...)` boundary declaration, code cannot conjure `Capital<USD>` out of a bare integer or string.

```rssc
transaction SplitRentThreeWays [audit: Z_SOX_302, date: "2015-09-01"] {
    // Source $1,000.00 linearly from Checking:
    let totalRent : Capital<USD> = credit OperatingChecking -> 1_000.00_USD;

    // $1,000.00 / 3 = $333.33 * 3 + $0.01 remainder!
    // FloorWithRemainder returns BOTH the 3 equal shares AND the 1-cent linear remainder:
    let (shares, remainder) = capital.splitEqual(totalRent, 3, RoundingPolicy.FloorWithRemainder);

    debit RoommateShareA <- shares[0]; // $333.33
    debit RoommateShareB <- shares[1]; // $333.33
    debit RoommateShareC <- shares[2]; // $333.33

    // REQUIRED: If we forget this line, finsc halts with FIN0005 because $0.01 was dropped!
    debit RoundingAdjustmentPool <- remainder; // $0.01 -> Total Debits == $1,000.00!
}
```

## Strongly Typed T-Accounts (`Account<TKind, TCurrency>`) {#account-kinds}

Every ledger account carries two compile-time type parameters:

| `TKind` Marker Type | Normal Balance | Accounting Equation Side | Increases On | Decreases On |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Asset` | Debit | Left ($\text{Assets} + \text{Expenses}$) | `debit` | `credit` |
| `Expense` | Debit | Left ($\text{Assets} + \text{Expenses}$) | `debit` | `credit` |
| `Liability` | Credit | Right ($\text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity} + \text{Revenue}$) | `credit` | `debit` |
| `Equity` | Credit | Right ($\text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity} + \text{Revenue}$) | `credit` | `debit` |
| `Revenue` | Credit | Right ($\text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity} + \text{Revenue}$) | `credit` | `debit` |

Because `TKind` is part of the static type signature, a helper function expecting an `Account<Expense, USD>` will never accidentally post into an `Account<Liability, USD>`!

## 128-Bit Scaled Fixed-Point Arithmetic (`FIN0003`) {#fixed-point-math}

In binary IEEE 754 floating-point (`float` / `double`), `0.1 + 0.2` evaluates to `0.30000000000000004`. Across millions of ledger rows, binary rounding drift corrupts trial balances.

- **Compile-Time Float Ban (`FIN0003`)**: Attempting to multiply, divide, or compare `Capital<T>`, `Account<K, T>`, or `Rate<A, B>` with `float` or `double` is a hard compile error (`FIN0003`).
- **Exact `Int128` Fixed-Point Representation**: Internally, `FinSharp.Runtime` represents monetary amounts as signed 128-bit integers (`System.Int128` on `.NET 10 / 11`) scaled by $10^8$ (`100,000,000` atomic ticks per major currency unit—supporting sub-basis-point interest and FX math while guaranteeing exact cent reconciliation at posting boundaries).
- **Explicit `RoundingPolicy` Enum**:
  - `RoundingPolicy.HalfEven` / `RoundingPolicy.Bankers` — Round half to even, returning `(roundedShare, adjustmentDelta)` inside settlement combinators.
  - `RoundingPolicy.FloorWithRemainder` — Deterministic floor division returning `(shares, exactRemainder)` as linear `Capital<T>` values.

## ISO 4217 Dimension-Typed Currencies (`FIN0004`) {#currency-dimensions}

Just as an aerospace compiler prevents adding meters to foot-pounds, Fin# treats every ISO 4217 currency (`USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `CAD`, `JPY`, `SGD`) and custom commodity unit (`MWh`, `TreasuryBill`) as a distinct phantom type dimension:

```rssc
// COMPILE ERROR FIN0004: Cannot combine Capital<USD> and Capital<EUR> without fx.convert!
// let invalidTotal = usdPayment + eurPayment;
```

To settle across currencies, see [`fx.convert(...)` in Ledgers & Transactions](ledgers-and-transactions.html#fx-settlement).

TOPIC: Ledgers, Accounts, Atomic Transactions & Z-SOX-302 Proofs [ledgers-and-transactions] (Language Specification)
================================================================================

# Ledgers, Accounts, Atomic Transactions & `Z-SOX-302` Proofs {#ledger-declarations}

In 1494, Franciscan mathematician **Luca Pacioli** formalized double-entry bookkeeping around a single conservation equation:

$$\text{Assets} + \text{Expenses} = \text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity} + \text{Revenue}$$

Every valid state transition in a closed accounting system preserves that equality because **the sum of debits in every journal entry equals the sum of credits** ($\sum \text{Debits} \equiv \sum \text{Credits}$). Fin# promotes Pacioli's 530-year-old equation directly into its grammar.

## Declaring a Closed `ledger` {#ledger-syntax}

A `ledger` block establishes a closed chart of accounts, its functional reporting currency, and its audit-attestation profile (`Z_SOX_302` or custom policy tags):

```rssc
ledger CampusAccessibilityFund [currency: USD, audit_standard: Z_SOX_302] {
    account GrantCashChecking   : Account<Asset, USD>;
    account EquipmentReceivable : Account<Asset, USD>;
    account AdaptiveGearExpense : Account<Expense, USD>;
    account VendorPayable       : Account<Liability, USD>;
    account DonorNetAssets      : Account<Equity, USD>;
    account WorkshopRevenue     : Account<Revenue, USD>;
}
```

> [!IMPORTANT] **Zero Mutation Outside `transaction` (`FIN0001`)**: An `Account<K, T>` exposes read-only query properties (`.id`, `.kind`, `.currency`, `.normalBalance`) in general functions, but **no `.Balance = ...` setter and no `+=` operator**. The *only* grammatical construct permitted to mutate account state is an atomic `transaction` (or boundary `opening_balance`) block!

## Boundary Ingress: `opening_balance(...)` {#boundary-ingress}

How does money enter a closed ledger when migrating an existing business or opening a fiscal year? Even at the boundary, capital never appears one-sided—`opening_balance` requires an explicit Asset/Liability pair balanced against an `Equity` (or Opening Balance Equity) account:

```rssc
opening_balance(
    debit:  GrantCashChecking,
    credit: DonorNetAssets,
    amount: 25_000.00_USD,
    memo:   "FY2016 Opening Endowment Balance"
);
```

## Atomic `transaction` Blocks {#atomic-transactions}

Every `transaction` block compiles to:
1. A **compile-time symbolic conservation check** (`FIN0002` + `FIN0005`), AND
2. A **runtime all-or-nothing atomic commit record** with deterministic SHA-256 hash chaining (`Z-SOX-302`).

### `debit` and `credit` Flow Arrows {#debit-and-credit}

Notice the directional visual symmetry of Fin#'s posting arrows:
- `credit <Account> -> <Amount>` **sources** linear `Capital<T>` from the credited leg.
- `debit <Account> <- <CapitalBinding>` **sinks** (consumes) linear `Capital<T>` into the debited leg.

```rssc
transaction InvoiceAndPayRampSupplier [audit: Z_SOX_302, date: "2015-09-14"] {
    // Leg 1: Accrue vendor invoice ($1,800.00)
    let invoiceObligation : Capital<USD> = credit VendorPayable -> 1_800.00_USD;
    debit AdaptiveGearExpense <- invoiceObligation;

    // Leg 2: Settle half ($900.00) immediately from checking
    let cashDisbursement : Capital<USD> = credit GrantCashChecking -> 900.00_USD;
    debit VendorPayable <- cashDisbursement;
}
```

In `InvoiceAndPayRampSupplier`, `finsc` verifies:
- Total `USD` Credits = `1,800.00 + 900.00 = 2,700.00_USD`
- Total `USD` Debits = `1,800.00 + 900.00 = 2,700.00_USD`
- Unconsumed linear bindings at `}` = `0` (`PASS`)!

## Multi-Currency FX Settlement Bridges (`fx.convert`) {#fx-settlement}

During the Summer 2015 Singapore arc of [*The Eleventh Child*](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie), household expenses in Singapore Dollars (`SGD`) had to reconcile cleanly against `USD` accounts without breaking single-currency conservation (`FIN0004`).

In Fin#, `fx.convert` routes cross-currency transfers through dual-currency FX clearing accounts so **both the `USD` sub-ledger AND the `SGD` sub-ledger remain 100% independently balanced**:

```rssc
transaction ReimburseSingaporeTransitCard [audit: Z_SOX_302, date: "2015-07-18"] {
    let quote = fx.quote<USD, SGD>(1.3685_0000, "2015-07-18T09:00:00Z", "MAS-Spot-Ref");

    let usdOutflow : Capital<USD> = credit UsdTravelChecking -> 100.00_USD;

    // Credits SgdFxClearing in SGD and debits UsdFxClearing in USD atomically:
    let (sgdProceeds, fxReceipt) = fx.convert(usdOutflow, quote, FxClearingBridge);

    debit SgdTransitCardAsset <- sgdProceeds; // Exact 136.85_SGD!
    audit.attach(fxReceipt);
}
```

# `finsc` CLI, Standard Library & `.NET` Compiler Architecture {#finsc-cli}

**Fin# (`FinSharp.Compiler` / `finsc`)** is architected as a clean, fast, 100%-readable self-hosted C# compiler frontend ("Mini-Roslyn" design) targeting **`.NET 10 / 11` CoreCLR and NativeAOT**—interoperating seamlessly with every `.NET` NuGet library while keeping build times under `3 seconds`.

## `finsc` Command-Line Interface Reference {#finsc-commands}

| Command | Flags & Arguments | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `finsc check <file\|dir>` | `--diagnostics=json`, `--strict` | Runs `Lexer` -> `Parser` -> `Binder` -> `LinearFlowAnalyzer` (`FIN0001`–`FIN0005`) in milliseconds without writing binaries. |
| `finsc build <project.finproj>` | `-o <dir>`, `--aot`, `--pdb` | Verifies all conservation proofs and lowers verified syntax trees via `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` (`Roslyn`) into deterministic `.dll` / `.exe` assemblies. |
| `finsc audit <ledger.fin>` | `--standard=Z_SOX_302`, `--json` | Executes ledger transactions deterministically and emits a SHA-256 Merkle trial-balance attestation report. |
| `finsc fmt <file\|dir>` | `--write`, `--check` | Comment-preserving source formatter that aligns `account`, `debit`, and `credit` columns cleanly. |
| `finsc lsp` | `--stdio` | Launches the JSON-RPC 2.0 Language Server providing real-time red squiggles for `FIN0001`–`FIN0005` and live T-account hover cards. |

## Standard Library Reference (`FinSharp.StdLib`) {#stdlib-overview}

### `capital.*` — Linear Allocation & Remainder Combinators {#capital-namespace}

| Function Signature | Return Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `capital.splitEqual(amount: Capital<T>, ways: Int32, policy: RoundingPolicy)` | `(Capital<T>[], Capital<T>)` | Consumes `amount` and returns `ways` equal shares plus an explicit linear `remainder` so zero sub-cents ever vanish (`FIN0005`). |
| `capital.allocateByWeights(amount: Capital<T>, weights: Int64[])` | `Capital<T>[]` | Consumes `amount` using deterministic Largest-Remainder (Hamilton) allocation guaranteed to sum to `amount` with zero leftover cents. |
| `capital.combine(left: Capital<T>, right: Capital<T>)` | `Capital<T>` | Consumes two same-currency bindings (`FIN0004` checked) and returns their exact 128-bit fixed-point sum. |
| `capital.assertZero(value: Capital<T>)` | `Unit` | Safely consumes a linear binding proven to equal `0.00` (for example, an exhausted loop accumulator). Traps in audit mode if non-zero. |

### `fx.*` — Multi-Currency Conservation Bridges {#fx-namespace}

| Function Signature | Return Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `fx.quote<TFrom, TTo>(scaledRate: Fixed128, timestampUtc: String, providerId: String)` | `Rate<TFrom, TTo>` | Creates an immutable, timestamped foreign-exchange quote using 8-decimal-place scaled fixed-point math (`FIN0003` float-free). |
| `fx.convert(source: Capital<TFrom>, quote: Rate<TFrom, TTo>, bridge: FxBridge<TFrom, TTo>)` | `(Capital<TTo>, FxAuditReceipt)` | Consumes `source` into `bridge`'s `TFrom` clearing leg and sources balanced `Capital<TTo>` from `bridge`'s `TTo` leg. |

### `audit.*` — `Z-SOX-302` Deterministic Attestation {#audit-namespace}

| Function Signature | Return Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `audit.trialBalance(ledger: Ledger)` | `TrialBalanceSnapshot` | Computes immutable period totals and asserts $\text{Assets} + \text{Expenses} \equiv \text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity} + \text{Revenue}$ per currency. |
| `audit.attestZsox302(ledger: Ledger, periodId: String)` | `ZsoxAttestation` | Emits SHA-256 hash-chained journal digest inspired by Zoë Wren Brooks's `Z-SOX-302` governance protocol in [*The Eleventh Child*](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie). |
| `audit.attach(receipt: AuditArtifact)` | `Unit` | Attaches structured FX, invoice, or external bank-feed evidence metadata to the enclosing `transaction` journal record. |

### `report.*` — Accessible Financial Statements {#report-namespace}

| Function Signature | Return Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `report.exportTaggedPdfUa(snapshot: TrialBalanceSnapshot, outputPath: String)` | `ReportResult` | Exports an ISO 14289-1 **Tagged `PDF/UA-1`** accessible trial balance and income statement compatible with screen readers and **RaggieSoft Document Studio**. |
| `report.exportCsv(snapshot: TrialBalanceSnapshot, outputPath: String)` | `ReportResult` | Exports RFC 4180 UTF-8 CSV ledger schedules with exact fixed-point decimal strings. |

## Compiler Pipeline Architecture ("Mini-Roslyn" on `.NET`) {#compiler-pipeline}

Why build `FinSharp.Compiler` as a standalone immutable C# syntax tree lowering to Roslyn rather than forking all 4+ million lines of `dotnet/roslyn`?

1. **Sub-3-Second Cold Builds**: Developers and contributors can clone, read, and compile the entire `Fin#` toolchain in seconds without a 30 GB compiler build environment.
2. **100-Level Read-Along Clarity**: Every pass—`FinLexer` -> `FinParser` -> `FinBinder` -> **`LinearFlowAnalyzer`** -> `CSharpRoslynEmitter`—fits cleanly in well-commented C# files.
3. **Full `.NET` & Studio Ecosystem Integration**: Emits standard signed `.NET` IL + PDBs and powers a candidate **RaggieSoft Fin# / Ledger Studio** workstation (`WebView2 + Monaco + Live T-Account Visualizer`, honoring `Community == 100% Architect Feature Parity`!).


================================================================================
TOPIC: Compiler Diagnostics Reference (FIN0001 – FIN0005) [diagnostics-reference] (Diagnostics & Proofs)
================================================================================

# Compiler Diagnostics Reference (`FIN0001` – `FIN0005`) {#diagnostics-overview}

Every conservation violation in **Fin#** is caught deterministically during `finsc check` and `finsc build`—long before code can touch a production database or ledger file. All diagnostics support `--diagnostics=json` and SARIF 2.1.0 output for CI/CD gates.

---

## `FIN0001`: `ConservationOfCapitalViolationException` {#fin0001}

- **Severity**: `Error` (Fatal Compile-Time Conservation Failure)
- **Named In**: [*Part 3: Question The Rules: The Birth of Fin#*](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie/fall-semester-2015/the-5-45-am-problem-the-birth-of-fin-home-on-geneva-street/part-3-question-the-rules-the-birth-of-fin) (`books/aubrie/e007/c001/p003.md`)
- **Cause**: Code attempted to mutate an `Account<K, T>` via scalar assignment (`=`, `+=`, `-=`), conjure an unpaired `Capital<T>` literal outside a boundary/credit leg, or mutate ledger state outside an atomic `transaction` block.

### Failing Example (`FIN0001`)

```rssc
// ERROR FIN0001: Unpaired scalar mutation outside an atomic transaction!
// Capital cannot be created out of thin air without a counterparty credit leg.
OperatingRevenue += 500_000_000.00_USD;
```

### Passing Fix

```rssc
transaction RecordVerifiedEnergyDelivery [audit: Z_SOX_302, date: "2015-08-26"] {
    let settledReceivable : Capital<USD> = credit OperatingRevenue -> 500_000_000.00_USD;
    debit AccountsReceivable <- settledReceivable;
}
```

---

## `FIN0002`: `UnbalancedJournalEntryError` {#fin0002}

- **Severity**: `Error`
- **Cause**: Inside a `transaction` block, the symbolic or concrete sum of `debit` postings does not equal the sum of `credit` postings for one or more currencies ($\sum \text{Debits} \neq \sum \text{Credits}$).

### Failing Example (`FIN0002`)

```rssc
transaction BrokenUtilitySplit [audit: Z_SOX_302] {
    let cash : Capital<USD> = credit OperatingChecking -> 120.00_USD;
    // Suppose a buggy custom helper tried to debit $125.00 against a $120.00 credit:
    debit ElectricUtilityExpense <- cash;
    debit InternetUtilityExpense <- credit OperatingChecking -> 5.00_USD; // Wait: if only one side posted -> FIN0002!
}
```

### Passing Fix

Ensure every `credit <Account> -> <Amount>` leg is paired 1-for-1 (or via conservation-preserving `capital.splitEqual` / `capital.combine` combinators) with `debit` legs summing to the exact same `Int128` scaled total.

---

## `FIN0003`: `BinaryFloatingPointForbiddenOnCapitalError` {#fin0003}

- **Severity**: `Error`
- **Cause**: An IEEE 754 binary floating-point type (`float` / `Single` or `double` / `Double`) was passed to or combined with `Capital<T>`, `Rate<A, B>`, or `Account<K, T>`.

### Failing Example (`FIN0003`)

```rssc
let badTaxRate : float64 = 0.053; // IEEE 754 binary float!
// ERROR FIN0003: Binary floating-point is banned from touching Capital<USD>.
let taxAmount = subtotal * badTaxRate;
```

### Passing Fix

Use exact 128-bit fixed-point `BasisPoints` / `Fixed128` literals (`5.30_pct` or `530_bps`) with an explicit `RoundingPolicy` so both the rounded tax share and sub-cent remainder are accounted for linearly!

---

## `FIN0004`: `CrossCurrencyConservationMismatchError` {#fin0004}

- **Severity**: `Error`
- **Cause**: Two `Capital<T>` or `Account<K, T>` operands with different ISO 4217 currency type arguments (such as `Capital<USD>` and `Capital<EUR>`) were combined directly without an auditable `fx.convert(...)` clearing bridge.

### Failing Example (`FIN0004`)

```rssc
// ERROR FIN0004: Cannot post Capital<SGD> into Account<Expense, USD>!
let sgdReceipt : Capital<SGD> = credit SingaporeCashWallet -> 42.00_SGD;
debit UsdDiningExpense <- sgdReceipt;
```

### Passing Fix

Route `sgdReceipt` through `fx.convert(sgdReceipt, quote, FxClearingBridge)` so both the `SGD` and `USD` sub-ledgers remain independently balanced.

---

## `FIN0005`: `UnconsumedLinearCapitalError` {#fin0005}

- **Severity**: `Error`
- **Cause**: A variable or tuple element of linear type `Capital<T>` (most commonly the `remainder` element returned by `capital.splitEqual`) reached the end of a lexical scope or conditional branch without being consumed by a `debit` posting or `capital.*` combinator.

### Failing Example (`FIN0005`)

```rssc
transaction DropPennyBug [audit: Z_SOX_302] {
    let dues : Capital<USD> = credit OperatingChecking -> 100.00_USD;
    // _ ignores the $0.01 remainder -> ERROR FIN0005!
    let (shares, _) = capital.splitEqual(dues, 3, RoundingPolicy.FloorWithRemainder);
    debit MemberA <- shares[0];
    debit MemberB <- shares[1];
    debit MemberC <- shares[2];
}
```

### Passing Fix

Bind `(shares, remainder)` and explicitly post `debit RoundingAdjustmentPool <- remainder;` before closing the `transaction` block.
